A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same evolving interpretability study, with retained VGGT experiments despite the broader title in v2. Inspection of all pages, including appendices, establishes that the text, equations, figures and references support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VGGT probing, attention-matching, knockout and input-perturbation experiments, including additional results in Appendices B–E.

after.justification: v2 retains original VGGT experiments and reports additional empirical analyses of DUSt3R and Depth Anything 3, real-world datasets, probe designs, feature matching and model sizes.

M1.justification: The core MLP probing, Sampson-loss and attention-knockout framework remains. v2 adapts probe inputs to averaged DUSt3R decoder features and two-/three-token triplet inputs, and adds a neighborhood/block knockout to the existing intervention family.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates controlled ShapeNet scenes. v2 adds DTU, ETH3D and MipNeRF360 geometric evaluations, SPair71k cross-scene semantic correspondence evaluation, and synthetic three-view configurations. These substantially broaden represented environments and task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds DUSt3R and Depth Anything 3 alongside VGGT in the comparative probing, attention and intervention analyses (Figs. 1–3). Appendix B.3 also adds a linear-probe comparator. SIFT and SuperGlue remain the comparators in the retained occlusion and scene-perturbation experiments.

E3.justification: The stated probe-training budget changes from 50 to 30 epochs; this establishes a reported setting change without proving which experiments were rerun. New experiments introduce dataset-specific splits and angular-bin sampling, one-epoch probe controls, DA3 size variants, and feature-matching evaluation with a three-patch tolerance.

E4.justification: v2 adds linear and one-epoch probe controls, triplet consistency, geometric versus semantic feature analyses, DA3 size analysis and block-level knockouts. Image-map and exact-patch interventions already existed in v1 Appendix D and are retained. Some earlier VGGT whole-head intervention combinations are no longer reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages, medians and failure rates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. Additional result entries in v2 do not change this reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive cross-model, real-world, probe-control and feature-matching results, including DUSt3R's earlier geometric emergence. Retained values also change: the VGGT layer-14/top-four-head knockout increase is 71.7 pixels in v1 Fig. 4 and 70.5 in v2 Fig. 3. Validation/symmetric probing curves and several knockout entries disappear. The occlusion, lighting, repetition and focal-length results are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the projection, essential/fundamental matrix, rank-two SVD projection and Sampson-error equations. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs; v2's new mechanistic explanations are empirical interpretations.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, contributions and conclusion broaden from understanding VGGT to identifying geometric mechanisms across VGGT, DUSt3R and DA3 on synthetic and real-world data. The conclusion also generalizes learned-prior behavior to multiple models, although the input-perturbation experiments remain VGGT-only.

C2.justification: v2 adds architectural explanations for layer timing and directional asymmetry, a semantic-to-geometric transition interpretation, and a proposed DINOv2/iBOT explanation for occlusion inpainting. It removes v1's explicit synthetic-texture bias and unidentified-classical-algorithm caveats. The qualification that knockout effects may involve mechanisms beyond correspondence matching remains.

D1.justification: Appendices A–D add ground-truth sources, real-dataset splits and sampling, triplet construction, feature-matching rules and intervention details. Validation-based early stopping and best-probe selection are newly documented. Conversely, v1's explicit VGGT checkpoint description, 518×518 input size and patch/token specifications are omitted.

R1.justification: The existing SfM, learned reconstruction and interpretability positioning remains. v2 adds discussion of Han et al.'s VGGT outlier analysis and Maggio et al.'s layer-based retrieval analysis, plus references supporting DA3, the additional datasets, DINOv2 and iBOT.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, model background and discussion are substantially rewritten around the broader study. Detailed scene-perturbation material moves from Section 5.2 to Appendix E, the appendices gain extensive subsection organization, and references move after the appendices.

P2.justification: v2 changes from two-column to single-column layout and reorganizes figures into multi-model, multi-dataset panels. Forward/reverse matching and intervention localities are consolidated into main-text displays, new analyses receive figures, and v1's separate focal-length plots are merged into v2 Fig. 21.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's single-model, synthetic-only geometric evidence through cross-architecture and real-world validation. Linear and one-epoch probe controls also strengthen the interpretation of decodable geometry. Some useful limitations and implementation disclosures disappear, and the broader learned-prior conclusion exceeds the VGGT-only perturbation evidence. Nevertheless, the expanded validation and controls provide a substantial net improvement in the support and generality of the central geometric findings.
